paragraphs.title: The Fall of Israel and the Exile of Samaria

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that Hoshea the son of Elah reigned over Israel in Samaria.
easy.q: Who reigned over Israel in Samaria?

easy.explanation: The verse says that Hoshea reigned nine years.
easy.q: How many years did Hoshea reign?

easy.explanation: The king of Assyria carried Israel away into Assyria.
easy.q: Where did the king of Assyria carry Israel?

answers: He became his servant and gave him presents
medium.explanation: Hoshea became Shalmaneser's servant and gave him presents.
medium.q: What did Hoshea do when Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against him?

answers: Because Hoshea sent messengers to Egypt and brought no present
medium.explanation: The king found conspiracy in Hoshea because he sent messengers to Egypt and stopped bringing the yearly present.
medium.q: Why did the king of Assyria imprison Hoshea?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the king of Assyria surrounding Samaria during the siege.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “besieged it” mean?

answers: Rebellion, Hoshea's imprisonment, siege, and capture
Siege, Hoshea's reign, rebellion, and exile
challenge.explanation: Hoshea rebelled, was imprisoned, Samaria was besieged for three years, and then Israel was carried away.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the fall of Samaria?

answers: Hoshea wanted to remain loyal to Assyria
Hoshea tried to break free from dependence on Assyria
Hoshea wanted the king of Egypt to rule Israel
challenge.explanation: His appeal to Egypt and refusal to bring presents show an attempt to resist Assyrian control.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Hoshea's sending messengers to Egypt instead of bringing presents to Assyria?

answers: The city was captured and Israel was exiled
Israel made a covenant with Egypt
challenge.explanation: After the three-year siege, the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away.
challenge.q: What was the direct result of the long siege of Samaria?

paragraphs.title: Israel's Sins and the Prophets' Warnings

easy.explanation: The passage says that they feared other gods.
easy.q: Whom did the children of Israel fear instead of the LORD?

easy.explanation: They built high places in all their cities.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel build in all their cities?

easy.explanation: The LORD testified against them by all the prophets and seers.
easy.q: Who warned Israel and Judah to turn from their evil ways?

medium.explanation: Verse 16 says that they served Baal.
medium.q: Which act is listed among Israel's sins?

answers: They would not hear and hardened their necks
medium.explanation: They would not hear and hardened their necks like their fathers.
medium.q: How did the children of Israel respond to the prophets?

medium.explanation: They followed vanity and became vain, turning to empty and worthless things.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “vanity” describe in this passage?

answers: The prophets' warnings versus the people's refusal to hear
The priests versus the kings of Judah only
challenge.explanation: The prophets warned the people, but the people refused to listen and continued in sin.
challenge.q: What central contrast does this passage present?

answers: The sin was a single isolated act
There was widespread and persistent abandonment of the LORD
The people kept the covenant faithfully
challenge.explanation: The passage lists idolatry, high places, Baal worship, divination, enchantments, and other offenses.
challenge.q: What does the long list of sins show about Israel's condition?

answers: Walking in the statutes of the heathen and burning incense as they did
challenge.explanation: Israel walked in the statutes of the heathen and practiced their religious customs.
challenge.q: Which act especially shows Israel copying the nations?

paragraphs.title: Divine Rejection and the Root of Israel's Sin

answers: He removed them out of his sight
easy.explanation: The passage says that the LORD was angry with Israel and removed them out of his sight.
easy.q: What did the LORD do to Israel because of their sins?

easy.explanation: The text says that there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.
easy.q: Which tribe remained after Israel was removed?

easy.explanation: The passage connects Israel's great sin with Jeroboam, the son of Nebat.
easy.q: Who made Israel to sin a great sin?

medium.explanation: Verse 19 says that Judah also kept not the commandments of the LORD.
medium.q: Who else did not keep the commandments of the LORD and walked in Israel's statutes?

answers: The LORD rent Israel from the house of David and they made Jeroboam king
The rise of the king of Assyria
medium.explanation: Israel's history is linked to being separated from the house of David and making Jeroboam king.
medium.q: How does the passage describe the historical beginning of Israel's sin?

medium.explanation: Israel was carried away from its own land to Assyria.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “was carried away” mean in this context?

answers: Walking in all the sins of Jeroboam and being driven away from the LORD
challenge.explanation: Israel continued in all the sins of Jeroboam and did not depart from them.
challenge.q: What is Israel's central sin according to this passage?

answers: Exile is presented as the result of the LORD removing Israel from his sight
Exile is presented as Israel's voluntary choice
challenge.explanation: The LORD removed Israel from his sight, and Israel was then carried away from its land.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect sin and exile?

answers: The warning was not limited to the northern kingdom
challenge.explanation: Judah also failed to keep the LORD's commandments and followed Israel's statutes.
challenge.q: What can be learned from mentioning Judah together with Israel?

easy.explanation: The king of Assyria brought people from several regions and placed them in Samaria.
easy.q: Who brought different peoples to dwell in the cities of Samaria?

easy.explanation: The LORD sent lions among them, and the lions slew some of them.
easy.q: What attacked the people who dwelt in Samaria?

answers: One of the kings of Israel
easy.explanation: The king of Assyria commanded that one of the priests be brought to teach them.
easy.q: Who was brought to teach the people the manner of the God of the land?

answers: They did not know the manner of the God of the land
They wanted to rebel against Assyria
medium.explanation: They said they did not know the manner of the God of the land, and therefore the lions attacked them.
medium.q: Why did the people ask the king of Assyria to bring them a priest?

medium.explanation: The priest came and dwelt in Bethel, where he taught the people.
medium.q: Where did the priest from Samaria dwell?

answers: The laws of the king of Assyria
The proper way to fear and worship the God of the land
medium.explanation: In context, the phrase refers to learning how to fear and worship the LORD.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “the manner of the God of the land” refer to?

answers: Their lack of fear was followed by the lions' attack, so a priest was brought to teach them
Their lack of fear caused the king of Assyria to leave
There is no connection between the events
challenge.explanation: Because the people did not fear the LORD, lions attacked them, and a priest was sent to teach them.
challenge.q: What is the cause-and-effect relationship between not fearing the LORD and the priest being sent?

answers: It included groups exiled from several different lands
challenge.explanation: The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim.
challenge.q: What can be inferred about the population living in Samaria?

answers: He was one of the kings of Assyria
He was familiar with the worship of the LORD in Israel
He belonged to one of the newly settled foreign peoples
challenge.explanation: The priest had been carried away from Samaria and was connected with Israel's worship of the LORD.
challenge.q: Why was an Israelite priest suited to teach the manner of the God of the land?

paragraphs.title: A Mixed Religion and Foreign Cults

answers: It made gods of its own and served them
It replaced them with worship of the LORD alone
easy.explanation: Every nation made gods of its own and placed them in the high places.
easy.q: What did each nation do concerning its own gods?

easy.explanation: The men of Cuth made Nergal.
easy.q: What did the men of Cuth make?

answers: They served only the king of Assyria
easy.explanation: They feared the LORD while also serving their own gods.
easy.q: What did the nations do in addition to serving their graven images?

medium.explanation: The men of Hamath made Ashima.
medium.q: What did the men of Hamath make?

answers: They burnt them in fire to their gods
They built high places for them
medium.explanation: The Sepharvites burnt their children in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech.
medium.q: What did the Sepharvites do to their children?

answers: Each nation had its own gods
All nations worshipped only one God
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that each people continued to worship its own gods.
medium.q: What does the phrase “every nation made gods of their own” mean?

answers: They feared the LORD while also serving their own gods
They did not worship any god
challenge.explanation: They feared the LORD but continued to serve their own gods and graven images.
challenge.q: Why is the religion of the people in Samaria described as mixed?

answers: The variety of religious practices in Samaria
Complete unity among all the peoples
The removal of the high places
challenge.explanation: The passage names different gods made by the different nations.
challenge.q: What does the listing of the different idols show?

answers: They feared the LORD but also served their graven images
They worshipped the LORD and knew no idols
They feared no god at all
challenge.explanation: The passage places their fear of the LORD alongside their continued service of idols.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in the verses describing these nations?

paragraphs.title: The Covenant Distinction between Israel and the Nations

easy.explanation: The covenant commanded Israel not to fear, bow to, serve, or sacrifice to other gods.
easy.q: What did the LORD command Israel not to do?

answers: The LORD who brought them out of Egypt
easy.explanation: They were commanded to fear and worship the LORD who brought them out of Egypt.
easy.q: Whom were the Israelites commanded to fear and worship?

answers: They feared the LORD and served their graven images
easy.explanation: The final verse says that they feared the LORD and served their graven images.
easy.q: What did the nations do unto that day?

answers: Exclusive loyalty to the LORD and obedience to his law
medium.explanation: The covenant required Israel to fear the LORD alone and observe his statutes, ordinances, law, and commandment.
medium.q: What did the covenant with Israel require?

medium.explanation: The text says that the LORD would deliver those who feared him out of the hand of all their enemies.
medium.q: What did the LORD promise to those who feared him?

medium.explanation: The phrase means to keep and carry out the statutes, ordinances, law, and commandment.
medium.q: What does “observe to do” mean in the context of the law and commandment?

answers: Israel was bound by covenant to worship the LORD alone, while the nations continued serving idols
The nations were more obligated than Israel
There was no difference between Israel and the nations
challenge.explanation: Israel was commanded to exclusive covenant faithfulness, while the nations mixed fear of the LORD with idol worship.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between Israel and the nations in this passage?

answers: To recall his deliverance and Israel's obligation to him
To explain the origin of Baal worship
To describe the exile of Samaria
challenge.explanation: The exodus showed the LORD's great power and gave Israel a reason to fear and worship him alone.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention the LORD bringing Israel out of Egypt?

answers: That the nations kept all the commandments of Israel
That the nations did not fully follow the covenant way
That the nations abandoned all their gods
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the nations continued in their former ways rather than obeying the LORD's covenant commands.
challenge.q: What does the repeated contrast between the nations' practices and the LORD's commandments emphasize?
